title: Wikidata grounding: the people with their own atlas entry
method: Each person was searched with the WikidataMCP semantic search (search_items), never the REST name search. One candidate was accepted only when its label, nationality and occupation matched the atlas entry; near-namesakes are listed in notes. Birth and death dates were then fetched for all accepted QIDs in one SPARQL query over P569/P570, and statement-level values were inspected where the query result looked wrong (Rodney) or imprecise (Pinchbeck). Wikidata content is CC0. Second pass, 2026-09-18: eight further person entries (Scott, Davis, Hunt, Hall, Davidoff, Higginbotham, Smith, Daston) were searched the same way, each candidate verified with get_statements before acceptance, and their dates fetched in one SPARQL query over P569/P570 with time precision; Daston's competing birth dates were resolved with get_statement_values on rank. Julia Cherry Spruill was re-tried and remains unmatched.

status_values.conflict: candidates disagree; needs a human decision

not_covered: The 786 people who appear only in rosters and strands are not in this pilot.

people.label: Julia Cherry Spruill
people.notes: Re-tried 2026-09-18 with three further vector-search queries ("Julia Cherry Spruill historian of colonial American women, Women's Life and Work in the Southern Colonies"; "Spruill author Women's Life and Work in the Southern Colonies 1938 University of North Carolina"; "Julia Cherry Spruill American woman historian southern colonies women's history pioneer 1938 book"). No candidate returned bore her name; results were unrelated American suffragists and clubwomen. Still unmatched: no Wikidata item appears to exist. Do not create a match from another source without review. Known dates (1899–1986) are not recorded here because they are not from a checked source.
